h1: Cabinet Painting in West Houston, TX
bodyHtml:
West Houston kitchens — in Memorial, the Energy Corridor, Briargrove, and Walnut Bend — often feature custom cabinetry and millwork worth preserving rather than replacing. A precise sprayed repaint updates the look, protects the wood, and keeps the craftsmanship, all for a fraction of new cabinetry. It is detailed work, and detail is what The Proud Paintbrush does.

We spray a hard, furniture-grade finish over genuine prep — degrease, sand, and bonding primer — for a result that reads custom up close.

West Houston Cabinets Deserve a Careful Hand

Many Memorial and Briargrove homes have solid-wood cabinets, raised-panel doors, and built-ins from the 1980s–2000s — exactly the cabinetry that rewards a meticulous spray finish over a rushed brush job. We mask and protect surrounding stone, hardwood, and high-end finishes, and we take the time these higher-value kitchens require.

Our Cabinet Painting Process

  • Label & remove — doors, drawers, and hardware tracked for an exact refit.
  • Degrease & sand — grease cut, surfaces scuffed, profiles hand-sanded.
  • Bonding primer — grips slick or previously finished surfaces; no chipping.
  • Spray, cure & reinstall — sprayed enamel cured between coats, refit and adjusted.

Preserving Craftsmanship Worth Keeping

A lot of Memorial and Energy Corridor kitchens were built with cabinetry you simply cannot buy off a shelf today — solid hardwood face frames, dovetailed drawers, raised-panel doors, and integrated built-ins fitted to the room. Ripping that out to install new stock cabinetry is often a downgrade in materials, and a custom replacement runs well into five figures. A meticulous sprayed repaint keeps every bit of that joinery and millwork while resetting the look, which is usually the better decision for both the home's character and its value. We approach these projects the way a furniture refinisher would: hand-sanding the profiles, working color into the panel details, and taking the time the doors need rather than rushing them off the rack. The result reads as the high-end cabinetry it already is, just current.

Color Matching and a Finish That Reads Custom

Homeowners in Briargrove and Walnut Bend often come to us with a designer color in hand or a stone counter they want the cabinets to play against, and we can match nearly any color and dial in the right sheen to suit it. On detailed raised-panel doors a satin or soft low-luster finish tends to flatter the millwork — it catches light along the profiles without the plastic-looking glare of a high gloss. Because we spray rather than brush, there are no ridges or lap marks in the field of the door, just an even, furniture-grade surface. We protect surrounding stone, hardwood, and high-end finishes throughout, and once cured the enamel wipes clean with mild soap and a soft cloth — no abrasives needed to keep it looking its best.

Why West Houston Homeowners Choose Us

We treat higher-value kitchens with the care they require, protect every surrounding finish, and back the work with our written warranty in Standard two-year and Premium five-year tiers — locally owned and insured since 2020. faqs.q: Do you paint custom cabinets and built-ins in Memorial?
faqs.a: Yes. Custom cabinetry, raised-panel doors, and built-ins are some of our favorite West Houston projects — they reward a careful, sprayed finish.

faqs.q: Will you protect my hardwood floors and stone counters?
faqs.a: Always. We mask and protect floors, countertops, backsplashes, and surrounding finishes before any prep or spraying begins.

faqs.q: Can you match a specific designer color?
faqs.a: Yes. We can match nearly any color and sheen, and we'll advise on durable cabinet finishes that hold up to daily use.

faqs.q: Is painting better than replacing custom Memorial cabinetry?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. The solid-wood, dovetailed cabinetry in many Memorial and Energy Corridor homes is better built than new stock units. A careful sprayed repaint preserves that craftsmanship and value for a fraction of a custom replacement.
